 How do you view Big Tech’s massive AI spending binge?
 
 Click here to take the poll and don't forget to share your thoughts in the WSB comments section . 
 
 
 
 
 
    
 
 
 
    
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Withdrawals resume: Binance users pull $3.6 billion after the biggest crypto heist.

 Debt dynamics: Fitch cuts France's outlook , citing borrowing costs and a wider deficit. 

 Prediction markets: Odds of Democrats sweeping the midterm elections hit 70% .
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Different playbook 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 Tech got wrecked last week as fears over AI spending, debt loads, and high valuations dominated the market narrative. Alphabet ( GOOGL ) lost half a trillion dollars in one session, Intel ( INTC ) recorded its worst trading day on record , while Microsoft's ( MSFT ) $25B bond sale and Meta's ( META ) $95B stock sale added to the worries. But as a new week begins, will the ghosts and scares that haunted investors fly away?

 Market test: The AI arms race is so expensive right now that even companies with deep pockets are borrowing heavily to fund it. Apple is unique among the hyperscalers, with an annual capex hovering around the $10B range, compared to the likes of Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta, which have each guided anywhere from $100B to $200B in capex for 2026. It has also weighed heavily on these giants, turning free cash flow negative across much of the group and drying up capital that previously went towards share buybacks and expanding dividends.

Apple ( AAPL ) is a different story. The iPhone maker has insulated its balance sheet and cash flows from the investor scrutiny that comes with it. However, it's a tradeoff. It carries the cost of relying on third-party frontier models and hyperscale cloud partners for high-end AI capabilities, and relinquishes control over compute architecture, inviting risks related to innovation and its ecosystem.

 So what's in focus?  Instead of AI, shareholders have narrowed in on Apple's product cycle. In the current fiscal first quarter, the company started shipping new touchscreen MacBooks, its smart hub called the HomeView, and the foldable iPhone Duo. Apple's earnings results and outlook today will help show whether these products, along with their AI features and its strong Services segment, can help the tech giant buck the capex concerns plaguing its rivals, as well as soaring memory costs . A lot is on the line, and Wall Street will size up the latest developments with new Apple CEO John Ternus hosting his first earnings call after the bell. Take the WSB survey.

 Free Webinar: Year-End Rally Watch - Fundamentals vs. FOMO 
 
 
 
 
 
 When stocks start climbing, the fear of missing out can be hard to ignore. And with midterm election years historically associated with strong year-end market performance, investors may be wondering whether another rally is on the horizon.

 But a rising market doesn't mean every stock is worth buying. How can you tell when momentum is supported by solid fundamentals, and when excitement is pushing prices beyond what the numbers justify?

 Join us today, November 2, at 4 PM ET for a free live webinar on navigating a potential year-end rally without getting caught up in the hype.

 We will explore historical market patterns, the risks of chasing momentum, and how a data-driven approach can help investors stay focused on earnings, profitability, and valuation rather than market sentiment alone.
